elements.label: Table 6.1
elements.description:
Table 6.1. Environment indicator, definitions

| Indicator | UNIT, DESCRIPTION | PERIOD OF DATA |
|---|---|---|
| Average topographical incline | Degree | 2017 |
| Air pollution | PM2.5 concentration (μg/m3) | Annual daily average over 2018 |
| Average settlement inundation depth in 1-in-100 year flood | Meter | 2020 flood model; 2015 Global Human Settlement Layers |
| Temperature | Celsius | Mean and variance over 2020 |
| Wind speed | Meter per second | Mean and variance over 2020 |
| Precipitation | Millimeter | Mean and variance over 2020 |
| Flood risk exposure | Share of the population exposed to high risk | 2020 flood model and 2020 population data |
| SPEI drought indicator | An SPEI of 0 indicates a value corresponding to 50% of the cumulative probability of D, according to a Log-logistic distribution." (D value is a threshold for drought, defined as precipitation minus evapo-transpiration). In sum, a higher SPEI corresponds to a higher probability of drought. | 2016–2021 average |

elements.label: Figure 6.6
elements.description:
Grouped vertical bar chart. Title: Figure 6.6. Share of districts with a high environmental risk factor, by district-level poverty rates. Y-axis: Share of districts with high risk (%), scale 0 to 100 (gridlines at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). X-axis categories: High poverty, Medium poverty, Low poverty. Legend series: At least one out of 6 risks; Precipitation (variance); Temperature (variance); Wind (variance); Air pollution (PM2.5); Share of population exposed to high flood risk; SPEI drought. No values are printed on the bars, so approximate readings are given.

High poverty: At least one out of 6 risks ~81; Precipitation (variance) ~26; Temperature (variance) ~26; Wind (variance) ~25; Air pollution (PM2.5) ~22; Share of population exposed to high flood risk ~11; SPEI drought ~27.

Medium poverty: At least one out of 6 risks ~87; Precipitation (variance) ~32; Temperature (variance) ~29; Wind (variance) ~39; Air pollution (PM2.5) ~28; Share of population exposed to high flood risk ~48; SPEI drought ~18.

Low poverty: At least one out of 6 risks ~84; Precipitation (variance) ~40; Temperature (variance) ~43; Wind (variance) ~35; Air pollution (PM2.5) ~50; Share of population exposed to high flood risk ~42; SPEI drought ~35.

The 'at least one risk' share is high across all groups and is highest for medium-poverty districts; the individual risks vary without a consistent monotonic pattern by poverty level, with flood exposure and air pollution highest in some groups and lowest in others.
